text:
jaz: Quick sync: staging showed tenants popping into hosted with no probe context and being served fallback models. Repro attached. Need a robust abstraction for probe trust across hosted/dedicated/private.

omar: saw that too. The sidecar->controlplane handoff is losing signal when sidecarless proxy path activates.

rita: high level: we need a safe way to assert 'this request is part of an active lease/probe' such that hosted can continue authz/serving decisions.

devin: options brainstormed: mTLS client cert on handoff, signed JWT assertion, opaque token sync, or explicit header re-injection (opt-in).

sun: header re-injection is simplest but weakest: anyone on the path could forge it. Should only be allowed with explicit tenant consent.

jaz: agreed. propose capability matrix:
- Trust mode A: mTLS cert provenance: sidecar presents a short-lived client cert (from tenant onboarding CA) when routing to hosted. Hosted validates cert chain and SAN lease-id. Works for connected/private deployments with TLS egress. Low CPU, low per-request latency.
- Trust mode B: Signed probe assertion (JWT-like) signed by tenant key (customer KMS or local HSM). Assertion is lease-scoped, valid for lease duration. Hosted verifies signature using exchanged trust anchor. Good for air-gapped setups after offline trust exchange. Higher CPU but can be cached per-lease.
- Trust mode C: Opaque sync token: private controlplane periodically pushes emitted tokens to hosted verification service over optional federation channel. Hosted validates the opaque token against cache. Works when outbound allowed, minimal crypto per-request.
- Trust mode D: Header re-injection: only for tenants who opt-in and explicitly accept risk; must be audited.

omar: mTLS is new compared to earlier thread. How do we provision the tenant CA? We could create a per-tenant short-lived CA cert signed by hosted admission CA at onboarding, or accept customer-provided CA during setup.

rita: provisioning options: (1) hosted-issued subordinate CA (auto-rotate), (2) customer-provided CA cert bundle (preferred for regulated customers), (3) offline exchange of verification fingerprints for signed assertions (air-gapped).

devin: implementation sketch for signed assertions: sidecar signs a compact assertion: {lease, issued_at, expires, probe_hint} -> JWS with kid referencing tenant pubkey. Hosted holds tenant pubkeys from onboarding and verifies. Cache the decoded assertion per-lease to avoid verify on every request.

sun: extra nuance: many private customers use customer KMS. We must not require hosted KMS. So support signing with customer private key (stored in their HSM) and exchange the public key or thumbprint during onboarding.

jaz: for air-gapped customers, onboarding will include one-time exchange of trust artifacts (public keys, cert bundles, or signed token batch) uploaded to hosted admin console by ops contact. That avoids runtime egress.

omar: backward compatibility: add manifest field probe_trust_mode: [mtls|signed_assertion|opaque_sync|header_optin]. If absent, default to strict: deny probe promotion (secure default).

rita: audit & observability: every time hosted admits a probe-derived route, emit event {tenant, lease, trust_mode, verifier_result, handed_off_by}. Also metric fallback.vs.probe_loss.

devin: perf: verify-once-per-lease. For mTLS path we can use TLS session cache and lease->session mapping. For signed_assertion route, cache verified assertion for lease TTL. For opaque_sync, hit local redis cache.

sun: edge cases: what if signed_assertion expires mid-lease? We should treat assertions as renewable; sidecar obtains refreshed assertion from local controlplane and replays it. Also define behavior when hosted cannot verify: fail closed (deny) vs fail open (serve public model) — default should be deny for security, but we can allow per-tenant policy to relax.

ojaz: small correction: default deny is consistent with secure defaults; if tenant explicitly opts for fail-open in manifest, we allow fallback with audit.

omar: migration plan:
1) Add manifest schema version + probe_trust_mode enum (v2 manifest).
2) Implement mTLS verification on hosted ingress + key exchange flow.
3) Add signed-assertion verifier and caching.
4) Add optional federation endpoint for opaque_sync.
5) Add transparent header-optin for consenting tenants (toggle in console).

rita: tests: unit verify for assertion signature, integration tests for sidecarless handoff, fuzz tests for forged headers, e2e with air-gapped onboarding file.

devin: UX: console needs a per-tenant "Probe trust" card showing current mode, last fallback timestamp, and ability to upload trust artifacts. Also surface a help doc describing trust tradeoffs.

sun: security review: I want to ensure we avoid key exfil risks from hosted when we store tenant pubkeys and cert bundles. Also ensure strict rate-limiting on federation verify endpoints.

infra-bot: ci-job handshake-probe-matrix queued -> job/handshake-matrix/v2 :white_check_mark:

jaz: action items:
- omar: draft manifest v2 PR with probe_trust_mode and optin semantics (2d)
- rita: write verification flow doc for mTLS and signed_assertion including onboarding UI (3d)
- devin: prototype assertion format and per-lease caching (2d)
- sun: security review on pubkey/cert storage and federation endpoints (3d)
- infra-bot: run handshake-probe-matrix and post results to thread

rita: one more: document policy for fail-open vs fail-closed in SLO/Sec annex.

jaz: agreed. We'll keep secure default and require explicit tenant opt-in for anything weaker. Sync tomorrow 9:30 to review drafts. Thanks.
